speaker: Doctor
text: I will ask you a few questions to better understand your condition. Can you describe the appearance of your rash on your palms, and how long have you been experiencing these symptoms?

speaker: Patient
text: 50-year-old male. The patient reports a year-long history of an itchy rash on his upper body and face. Additionally, he has been experiencing a numbness and tingling sensation on both palms. He has been working on his family's rice farm, also caring for livestock.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Porphyria Cutanea Tarda (PCT). The combination of a longstanding pruritic rash on sun-exposed areas (face/upper body), sensory neuropathy (numbness/tingling), and risk factors for iron overload (livestock exposure, potential hemochromatosis) is highly characteristic of PCT, which is often triggered by alcohol, hepatitis C, or estrogen therapy. I need to confirm the presence of blistering or skin fragility and check for liver function abnormalities. REQUEST TEST: Liver function panel, CBC, Iron studies, and Uroporphyrin levels.
